text:
mari: Heads-up — found a cancellation/timeout leak in the Kotlin SDK sample app when using Retrofit suspend wrappers + custom retry interceptor on Android 13. Repro and notes below.

jon: short description?

mari: when we wrap Call.execute() in withContext(Dispatchers.IO) inside a suspend helper, coroutine cancellation doesn't cancel the underlying OkHttp call. On low-memory/emulator the app keeps executing network work even after timeouts/cancellation and the retry interceptor clones the request leading to duplicate in-flight calls.

sam: does this only happen with execute() or with enqueue() too?

mari: repro uses blocking execute() inside withContext. snippet: 
```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call<T>.awaitBlocking(): Response<T> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
  try { execute() } catch (e: IOException) { throw e }
}
```

rachel: ah yeah. withContext won't interrupt a blocking native call. OkHttp's Call.cancel() must be invoked on the Call to interrupt. If coroutine is cancelled you need to register a cancellation handler to call.cancel().

jon: we have a RetryInterceptor that does: if (needRetry) { val clone = call.clone(); clone.execute() } — that assumes execute() returns when cancelled. If execute() is stuck the interceptor will spin or block dispatcher.

mari: exact symptoms: 1) UI triggers cancel (e.g., user navigates away) but the network thread keeps doing work, 2) subsequent retry attempts spawn clones, 3) server sees duplicates, 4) metrics show high tail latency and increased token usage.

sam: any stacktraces?

mari: attached in repo gist but common pattern: threads stuck inside Okio read or socket read after connect, while coroutine job is cancelled.

rachel: suggested fix in sample app: provide a suspend-friendly extension that ties coroutine cancellation to call.cancel():
```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call<T>.awaitCancellable(): Response<T> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
  enqueue(object: Callback { ... call cont.resume(...) ... })
}
```

jon: also add guard in RetryInterceptor to avoid cloning synchronous call objects on the same dispatcher — use a bounded threadpool or schedule retries on a separate executor.

mari: patched sample app branch: uses awaitCancellable extension, updates retry to use call.clone() only on a dedicated retry executor, and adds tests that cancel jobs after 100ms. Repro test simulates 30 concurrent requests.

sam: can you add an SDK docs blurb titled "Retrofit/OkHttp: cancellation and retry pitfalls on Android"? Include examples and the awaitCancellable pattern.

mari: will open PR with sample, docs, and a tiny runbook entry describing how to recognize (lots of blocked threads in okhttp, duplicate server requests, increased token counts).

deploy-bot: note: SDK 3.5.2 will include OkHttp 4.11 that exposes call.timeout() & improved cancel behavior — still worth shipping sample/docs.

mari: good call. I'll verify against 3.5.2 and include compatibility note for Android <12 where socket interrupt behavior differs. Thanks all :raised_hands:
